chapter_note: Chapter is heavily damaged (88.9% damage ratio) but retains a clear bilayered structure: an opening polemical/dialogue frame in which a disciple cites the Magousaean (Zoroastrian) teaching about a fourteen-headed dragon and asks whether it is somatic or pneumatic, followed by a substantial cosmological substrate teaching that maps the dragon onto the human body — seven heads above (the seven sense-organs on the foremost-bust: two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, mouth/tongue) and seven below (haunches etc.), with five 'caves' (mouth, throat, ...). The substrate enumeration is intact in i=22-48. The soteriological closure (i=49-52) brings in 'elect' vocabulary (institutional) and the closing dialogue (i=53-62) is the apostolic frame. The strong editorial fatigue toward cosmological_substrate in second half reflects the substrate teaching displacing the early polemic.
